features.name: Worktree Lanes
features.behavior: Add git-worktree-based parallel lanes so multiple features can be developed concurrently without file collisions: `lane-new`/`lane-list`/`lane-land`/`lane-drop` tooling that creates sibling-directory worktrees on `lane/<feature-id>` branches, and arch-002 re-scoped from repo-wide WIP=1 to per-lane WIP=1 (the active feature is detected relative to the current git branch, not the whole feature_list.json).
features.verification: npm run check passes; check-arch enforces per-lane WIP=1 so two lanes may each have a different active feature without violating the rule; a simulated two-worktree session (two sibling checkouts on two `lane/*` branches) each pass check and check-arch independently, and clean-state-check stays correctly scoped to its own worktree.

features.name: Sharded Feature State
features.behavior: Split the mutable per-feature fields (state, evidence, owner, timestamps) out of feature_list.json into one file per feature under .harness/state/<id>.json, so two lanes landing different features never touch the same tracked path and merge without conflict by construction. feature_list.json keeps only declaration fields (id, name, behavior, dependencies, layers). verify-feature, session-trace, and harness-report read/write the shard files instead of rewriting the whole feature list.
features.verification: npm run check passes; verify-feature reads and writes only its own feature's shard file (never the shared feature_list.json); a simulated two-lane merge (two branches each updating a different feature's shard under .harness/state/) merges with zero conflicts; harness-report aggregates state correctly across all shards.

features.name: Upgrade Backups
features.behavior: Before harness-upgrade overwrites mustNotEdit CORE surfaces, snapshot the current on-disk state of every file about to be touched: checksum-deduped (skip a redundant backup when nothing changed), gzip-compressed per file, stored in .harness/backups/<id>/ (gitignored — a local safety net, not durable evidence). Retention keeps the 5 most recent unpinned backups; pinned backups are never pruned. backup-list/backup-pin/backup-unpin/backup-restore (restore accepts an id or "latest") round out the command surface. Restore is per file: existed=true writes the snapshotted content back, existed=false removes a file the operation newly created.
features.verification: npm run check passes; unit tests cover snapshot creation (including existed=false files), dedup, restore fidelity (including the existed=false removal case), and prune/pin interaction; the adoption matrix's upgrade test asserts a real upgrade() call creates a backup and that restoring it reproduces the pre-upgrade (corrupted) state before re-upgrading to leave the repo fixed.

features.name: Dogfooding Feedback Round 1
features.behavior: Three quick, low-risk fixes from real-world adopter feedback (DOGFOODING-FEEDBACK-payroll.md Tier 1), each tied to an incident that actually happened: (1) check-arch warns (does not fail) when untracked-but-not-gitignored files exist, since coverage rules like arch-005 only see git-tracked files and this caused two real CI breaks in an adopter project; (2) a new add-feature <id> <name> command appends a correctly-shaped, declaration-only feature stub, replacing the hand-rolled node -e JSON construction the adopter repeated 11+ times; (3) the lint layer fails on a duplicate or missing session number in PROGRESS.md's ### Session N headers (checked as a set, not file order, so a legitimate out-of-order hotfix write is not flagged) — the adopter's log accumulated a real duplicate session number that nothing ever caught.
features.verification: npm run check passes; unit tests cover the untracked-file warning (present/absent/no-git-repo), add-feature (stub shape, duplicate-id rejection, multi-word name handling), and the progress-log check (sequential, out-of-order-but-valid, duplicate, gap, no-sessions-yet cases).
